description: Somos un grupo de estudiantes universitarios de San luis interesados en el espacio y el diseño de niveles realcionados con la ciencia.
summary:
We created a game about unmanned space missions where engineering and science become entertaining, allowing the player's creativity to find multiple solutions to overcome obstacles and reach Mars.
Our greatest achievement was making complex data easily accessible to any user, regardless of their technical background. This is important because it brings real space exploration closer to the general public. By translating challenging scientific parameters into visual and engaging decisions, we inspire technological vocations and demonstrate that understanding how the universe works does not have to be complicated.
details:
We have developed a game that integrates three fundamental pillars: applied engineering, scientific rigor, and entertainment. It is an interactive simulation in which the player takes on the role of designing, planning, and managing realistic unmanned space missions, navigating interconnected variables such as mass, budget, energy consumption, and orbital mechanics to replicate an authentic unmanned space mission.

Our primary objective is to democratize knowledge about how space exploration truly works, bridging the gap between complex science and the general public. We aim to spark genuine curiosity for science, technology, and engineering by showcasing not only the final achievements typically seen in the news, but also the behind-the-scenes design, calculation, and decision-making processes that make a mission successful. By allowing players to experience firsthand the management of limited resources and real-world problem-solving, the game serves as an active learning tool where failure does not frustrate, but rather teaches how the laws of physics and engineering interact in a space environment.

This initiative is designed with teenagers and young adults in mind—both men and women—regardless of their prior academic background (ranging from those who have not yet completed secondary education to those currently pursuing technical or university degrees). We target anyone interested in understanding space and the operation of probes and satellites in a direct, visual, and intuitive way, whether they approach the game out of pure curiosity and leisure or as a practical educational supplement. Ultimately, we seek for this experience to serve as an initial spark that inspires future scientific and technological vocations, bringing younger generations closer to the real opportunities offered by the space sector.

─────────── ⋆⋅☆⋅⋆ ───────────

Deep Space

Build for the mission. Launch with precision.

We propose an idle-style game in which the player is accompanied by Alex, an astronaut who briefs them on the mission to be accomplished. The player must complete it to earn a reward; if they fail, they will lose the invested funds, whereas if they manage to fulfill at least one secondary mission objective, they will be able to recover part of the resources or advance in their research.

To perform launches, the user will initially have access to the Saturn V spacecraft, with the ability to upgrade to the Falcon Heavy and, eventually, acquire the Starship. Furthermore, each spacecraft will feature its own dedicated upgrades, such as:

Power:

☆Solar panel optimization

Propulsion:

☆Liftoff velocity enhancements

Protective Lenses:

☆Optical lens upgrades to make them radiation-resistant

Shielding:

☆External shielding reinforcement

☆Replacement of materials with more durable alternatives

However, all of these upgrades come at a cost. Prior to launch, the player must not only evaluate whether they have the necessary funds (Astracoins), but also ensure that the rocket does not exceed its maximum payload capacity and verify that the spacecraft carries sufficient fuel to complete the mission.

The various missions the player must overcome:

Throughout the game, the player must complete different phases and missions of increasing complexity: they will begin by launching an Earth reconnaissance satellite, and then advance to a probe that maintains communication with Earth and transmits data. They will also gain access to a space telescope to capture long-range images. As they progress, they will reach the Moon and Mars: in the lunar phase, they must first deploy a reconnaissance satellite and a probe that collects and transmits data to Earth, subsequently executing a lunar landing with a Rover. Finally, when attempting to reach Mars, they will have to replicate and refine this same process, with the ultimate goal of the game being to achieve a successful landing on Mars with a Rover.

─────────── ⋆⋅☆⋅⋆ ───────────

What tools did we use to create the game?

The game was programmed entirely in Godot, a free, lightweight, and open-source game engine.

Why did we choose this tool?

Because it offers key features that streamline development:

☆Node and scene architecture: The entire project is structured by combining fundamental building blocks into modular, reusable scenes.

☆Dedicated 2D engine: It features a native 2D environment that operates directly in pixels, making it ideal for our visual style.

☆Agile programming: It uses GDScript, a flexible language designed specifically for video game development.

☆Built-in tools: It includes an integrated animation editor and a comprehensive user interface (UI) design system without relying on external software.

The game's source code is available on GitHub.

─────────── ⋆⋅☆⋅⋆ ───────────

What do we propose?

The project proposes an interactive experience that combines elements of entertainment and learning through the simulation of space missions. Its objective is to represent, in a realistic yet simple and accessible manner, the key factors that must be taken into account when designing a space mission project: from the initial budget required to launch the project to the limitations and advantages offered by each vehicle. Through the game's mechanics, the goal is for the player to indirectly acquire knowledge about various spacecraft, satellites, rovers, and other key elements throughout the history of space exploration, as well as to understand their purpose within a mission and how they operate. We have built a world in which a single decision can alter the entire course of the mission; each player will learn about the challenges of space missions and the requirements necessary to sustain them over time.

The visual aesthetic is based on a pixel-art style, paying homage to classic computer video games. A limited color palette restricted to blue and orange tones was chosen—complementary colors that help maximize contrast and visual detail, while also reinforcing the overall atmosphere.

Furthermore, compared to other video games, what sets it apart is the way it translates complex information into a straightforward format, allowing the user to understand it without requiring any prior knowledge of the subject.

─────────── ⋆⋅☆⋅⋆ ───────────

Factors Taken into Account:

We considered multiple factors during the creation and development of the game. Among them, our goal was to make it accessible to people with varying levels of space knowledge—from none to advanced—so that anyone could not only be entertained, but also learn.

We also took into account the real-world challenges faced by space missions beyond what is typically portrayed, such as resource management, spacecraft mass, component efficiency, and, ultimately, the planning of each mission. We wanted player decisions to have consequences and for them to learn through experimentation, including making mistakes.

Additionally, we sought to combine strategy, management, and adventure into an engaging visual experience using a pixel-art style. Finally, we incorporated the use of open data from NASA and other space agencies related to space mission design and planning to ground the game's mechanics in real-world information and concepts.

In short, our objective was to create a game that sparked curiosity, encouraged learning, and brought space exploration closer to all types of players..

─────────── ⋆⋅☆⋅⋆ ───────────

What benefits does the game offer?

Our game offers an experience that enables learning through practice and experimentation. Players develop key skills such as strategic thinking, problem-solving, planning, and resource management, while discovering how their decisions can influence the outcome of a space mission.

Furthermore, it provides them with the opportunity to experiment freely, test different solutions, and learn from their mistakes without real-world consequences. Our goal is to spark curiosity about science and space exploration by transforming complex concepts into interactive and accessible challenges.

In this way, the player not only acquires new knowledge, but also develops practical tools to analyze situations, make informed decisions, and tackle problems effectively.

─────────── ⋆⋅☆⋅⋆ ───────────

What is the expected impact of the project?

The impact we seek to generate with our project is to bring knowledge about space and space exploration closer to a wider audience, sparking curiosity and interest in science and technology.

Through an interactive and accessible experience, we want more people to discover the challenges involved in developing a space mission and feel motivated to learn, research, and explore these topics on their own.

In the long term, we hope the game serves as a gateway to scientific knowledge, demonstrating that learning about space can be an entertaining, participatory, and inspiring experience.

¡¡Note for the Jury!!

Since it's a game developed by us, it doesn't have a company license, which causes Windows antivirus to give a warning when trying to run the playable version of the game. You can disable the firewall, run it as an administrator (it might fail once or twice with this method), or in the warning notification itself, you might get the option to 'run anyway'.
